answer_sql:
SELECT
  p.brand,
  ROUND(SUM(s.gross_amount), 2) AS gross_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON s.product_key = p.product_key
WHERE
  s.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND s.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
GROUP BY
  p.brand
ORDER BY
  net_revenue DESC

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: For each of the eleven brands Contoso sells under, the two 2024 revenue figures side by side in USD: gross — what the goods would have fetched at list price — and net, what customers were actually charged after discount. A sale counts as 2024 when the order was placed between 1 January and 31 December 2024, and both sales channels are included, the physical shops and the web shop. Eleven brands, one row each, ordered by net. Together they took 33,631,448.47 gross and 31,639,690.92 net over 38,109 order lines; the 1,991,757.55 between those two totals is discount, which in this warehouse is the whole of the difference between gross and net. Contoso (6.57m net) and Adventure Works (6.42m) are nearly level at the top; the bottom three are an order of magnitude smaller, Tailspin Toys taking 241,721.03. The erosion from gross to net is strikingly even — 5.79% to 6.45% of gross for ten of the eleven — with one exception a reader should see: Northwind Traders discounted just 3.83%, keeping noticeably more of its list value than any other brand. WHAT IS NOT IN THESE FIGURES: no returns, credits, taxes, shipping or any other finance deduction, because none of those is recorded anywhere in this bundle. "Net" here means after-discount only, and is therefore HIGHER than a finance-grade net revenue would be. This is also not a fiscal year, and not a gross-to-net bridge showing each deduction as its own line.

value.asks: Compare gross vs net revenue by brand
value.sql:
SELECT
  p.brand,
  ROUND(SUM(s.gross_amount), 2) AS gross_revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
JOIN contoso_served.dim_product AS p
  ON s.product_key = p.product_key
WHERE
  s.order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
  AND s.order_date < CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
GROUP BY
  p.brand
ORDER BY
  net_revenue DESC
value.means: For each of the eleven brands Contoso sells under, the two 2024 revenue figures side by side in USD: gross — what the goods would have fetched at list price — and net, what customers were actually charged after discount. A sale counts as 2024 when the order was placed between 1 January and 31 December 2024, and both sales channels are included, the physical shops and the web shop. Eleven brands, one row each, ordered by net. Together they took 33,631,448.47 gross and 31,639,690.92 net over 38,109 order lines; the 1,991,757.55 between those two totals is discount, which in this warehouse is the whole of the difference between gross and net. Contoso (6.57m net) and Adventure Works (6.42m) are nearly level at the top; the bottom three are an order of magnitude smaller, Tailspin Toys taking 241,721.03. The erosion from gross to net is strikingly even — 5.79% to 6.45% of gross for ten of the eleven — with one exception a reader should see: Northwind Traders discounted just 3.83%, keeping noticeably more of its list value than any other brand. WHAT IS NOT IN THESE FIGURES: no returns, credits, taxes, shipping or any other finance deduction, because none of those is recorded anywhere in this bundle. "Net" here means after-discount only, and is therefore HIGHER than a finance-grade net revenue would be. This is also not a fiscal year, and not a gross-to-net bridge showing each deduction as its own line.

readings.declaration: net_amount is 'what the customer was actually charged for the line, in USD, after discount', and discount_amount is measured as exactly gross_amount - net_amount — so discount is provably the entire gap between the two columns I am showing. No return, credit, tax or freight column exists on any relation here, so the fuller readings are not computable at all; the question's own cannot_express names the full bridge as out of reach. A limit of the data, not a choice I made between available figures.
